nodes.title: hero-synergy v0.1.0, fully decided
nodes.body:
## Destination

hero-synergy v0.1.0 fully decided: every question it depends on is resolved and every hard-to-reverse default has been challenged, so the result goes straight to `/to-spec`.

The product is the VS Code Cockpit described in [the seed](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#destination). Its five capabilities are the outer bound: a ticket may cut one down, but nothing is added.

## Notes

- **Domain.** An unofficial VS Code cockpit for Matt Pocock's agent skills. The glossary is [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CONTEXT.md). The reference material is [`docs/seed.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md), frozen on 2026-10-02; this map replaces its Decisions so far, Not yet specified and Out of scope sections.
- **Plan, don't build.** This map decides; the build comes afterwards through `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets` and `/implement`. Two exceptions: [Scaffold the workspace](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/2) lands on `main`, and prototypes are throwaway work on `prototype/<name>` branches linked from their ticket.
- **Seed tags.** `[E]` items are requirements. These `[P]` defaults stand as decided without a ticket: principles 1 to 6, the Vue 3 webview, `extensionKind: workspace`, spawning the user's `claude` with the Agent SDK as fallback, action discovery from `SKILL.md` frontmatter, Changesets fixed versioning with one combined release, and the unofficial branding. Every other `[P]` is challenged by a ticket here.
- **Skills.** Grilling tickets use `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling`. Prototype tickets use `/prototype`. Research tickets use `/research` and save findings as `docs/research/<name>.md` on a `research/<name>` branch.
- **Writing to the repo.** Decided in [How do a session's worktree edits get back to main?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/5) and [ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md): every ticket session works in its own git worktree, never in the shared checkout, and pushes its own glossary and ADR edits to `main` when the ticket closes, following the routine in `CLAUDE.md` (install, build, `vp check --fix`, commit, rebase onto `origin/main`, push `HEAD:main`; no PR). Research branches are pushed and linked from their ticket; prototypes stay on their branch.
- **ADRs.** Only for a decision that is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off. They live in `docs/adr/`.
- **Toolchain.** Use `vp` for everything; never call oxlint, oxfmt or vitest directly. The devcontainer has no global `vp`, so run the project's own: `pnpm exec vp <command>`. CI runs `vp check`, which also formats Markdown: run `vp check --fix` before pushing anything to `main`, glossary and ADR edits included.
- **Driver.** Eduardo (`dbarjs`). A claim is an assignment to him.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket: the gist, then the link -->
- [Which wayfinder conventions exist in the wild?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/10) — three generations upstream (single file, early tracker map, current map); old forms are recognizable by headings and `Status:` lines, legacy claim labels were never released, and the tracker templates still lag behind `SKILL.md`
- [Are the hero-synergy names free on npm, the Marketplace and Open VSX?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/8) — the npm organization exists (almost certainly Eduardo's, unconfirmed); the unscoped npm name, both Marketplace publisher IDs and both Open VSX namespaces look free; the publisher ID can never be changed
- [Can one GraphQL query collect everything the scout needs?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/9) — yes: one query returns a whole map for 6 rate-limit points, but `updatedAt` doesn't move when a parent or blocker is added, so relationships must be collected fresh every time
- [How do VS Code terminals and Claude Code hooks behave on Windows?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/11) — by reading only: shell quoting, npm `.cmd` shims and a missing `SessionEnd` are the Windows risks; running `claude` as the terminal's own process avoids the quoting, and twelve items still need a real Windows test
- [How can a VS Code extension be integration-tested under Vite+?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/13) — extension-host tests need Mocha through `@vscode/test-cli` as a separate script beside `vp test`; the webview is tested as a Vue app outside VS Code; real end-to-end means experimental Playwright on Electron
- [Which VS Code versions do Cursor, Windsurf and VSCodium ship?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/12) — VSCodium is on 1.135, Cursor on 1.128, Windsurf on 1.126; the recommended floor is `^1.105.0`, set by the extension host's Node version rather than by any API
- [Scaffold the workspace](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/2) — on `main` and green in CI: Vite+ 1.0.0, Node 26.10, pnpm 12.8.1 and TypeScript 7 work together; the seed needed fourteen small corrections (missing `@vitejs/plugin-vue`, `@types/node`, `activationEvents` and a pnpm `allowBuilds` decision among them), and the devcontainer can't install the global `vp`
- [Which publisher ID and npm names?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/19) — publisher `dbarjs` (created), so the extension ID is `dbarjs.hero-synergy` and the Open VSX namespace is `dbarjs`; the bare name `hero-synergy` belongs to the extension, the unscoped npm name is not claimed, and `@hero-synergy/core` and `@hero-synergy/cli` stand
- [Do the status hooks report a session's state reliably?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/6) — yes, with a corrected table: the plugin stays and also hooks tool calls, `PermissionRequest` replaces the 6-second-late notification and tells a question from an approval, the terminal closing is the truth for "ended", and Esc is an accepted gap shown as time since the last status event
- [Does @effect/vitest 4 work with Vitest 5 under Vite+?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/14) — yes, with no override and no peer warning: it shares the one Vitest 5.0.1 that Vite+ pins, on Node 24 and 26; Effect tests import from `@effect/vitest` instead of `vite-plus/test`
- [Which trackers and workspace shapes does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/3) — GitHub on github.com with native relationships, and local markdown; one repo per window, every open map shown; the tracker doc's heading decides which tracker is read; GitLab, "Other" trackers, closed maps and multi-root grouping are cut
- [What ships in v0.1.0 besides the extension?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/4) — only the extension: the CLI is cut and its package removed, `@hero-synergy/core` stays a private workspace package bundled into the extension, nothing goes to npm, and Nitro has no role
- [zod or Effect Schema for the snapshot?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/15) — Effect Schema for all boundary data, and zod is dropped: both libraries feed `claude -p --json-schema` and cost about 25 KB gzipped in the webview, so one library is enough; boundary data is plain JSON, the webview imports types only, and core exports no schema objects ([ADR 0002](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-effect-schema-models-all-boundary-data.md))
- [How do a session's worktree edits get back to main?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/5) — every ticket session gets `claude -w` and pushes its own edits straight to `main` after a rebase; the Cockpit never runs git or writes to the tracker, only shows each worktree's uncommitted and unpushed state ([ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md))
- [Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/17) — VS Code `^1.105.0` (`@types/vscode ~1.105.0`) on macOS and Linux, WSL remote as the Windows route, native Windows best-effort, forks not blocked but unsupported via Open VSX; README states Claude Code ≥ 2.1.139 and Node ≥ 22.18 on `PATH`; a session runs `claude` as the terminal's own process, never through a shell; no gating on editor or OS

## Not yet specified

- **The snapshot's fields.** What a snapshot holds for each map and ticket, and which fields are facts from the tracker rather than a model's reading. It has to fit both trackers: a ticket is a URL on GitHub and a file path on a local tracker, and a local claim has no person. Waits on [Which wayfinder conventions exist in the wild?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/10) and [Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/16).
- **The scout budget.** Refresh cadence, bundle size limits, cache keys, behavior on rate limits, and a fallback if `--safe-mode` changes. Waits on [Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/16).
- **Scout against status hooks.** When a session has claimed a ticket and the tracker doesn't show it yet, which side the Cockpit believes, and for how long. Status belongs to the ticket and its terminal, not to a session id, which changes on `/clear`. Waits on [Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/16).
- **Actions in the Cockpit.** Where actions sit, how the command is shown, and how the command name follows the install route (plugin or skills.sh). Waits on [How do maps render in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/7).

## Out of scope

- **Building and releasing v0.1.0.** The build, the release pipeline run and the one-time registry setup happen after this map.
- **A polished README for the extension and the repository.** Comes after the v0.1.0 release; the release ships with the plain README the platform decision asks for. Tracked outside the map in [Write a polished README for the extension and the repository](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/22).
- **From the seed, for v0.1.0:** a TUI; Claude Code's agent view; the official Claude Code VS Code extension; sandcastle and container sandboxes; agents other than Claude Code; writing to the tracker from the Cockpit; chaining user-invoked skills automatically; telemetry; a hosted service.
- **Trackers and workspace shapes, for v0.1.0:** GitLab; "Other" trackers and the agentic collect step; any promise for GitHub Enterprise Server, the text fallbacks or cross-repo relationships; grouping maps per folder or a repo picker in a multi-root workspace; a folder holding several repos; closed maps. Ruled out in [Which trackers and workspace shapes does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/3).
- **Beyond the extension, for v0.1.0:** the `@hero-synergy/cli` package and its commands; `@hero-synergy/core` as a public npm package; anything published to npm; Nitro, a browser Cockpit and a docs site. Ruled out in [What ships in v0.1.0 besides the extension?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/4).
- **Platform verification, for v0.1.0:** the twelve-item real-Windows test from the Windows research, and verifying terminals, icons and webview views inside Cursor, Devin Desktop and VSCodium. Ruled out in [Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/17).

nodes.title: Scaffold the workspace
nodes.body:
## Question

What does the repo look like once the seed's stack is actually installed, and what did installing it reveal that the seed got wrong?

This is a task ticket (AFK): do the work, then record what was done and the facts later tickets depend on.

## Work

- Install Vite+ and pin Node 26 and pnpm 12, following [Getting started](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#getting-started) in the seed.
- Create `packages/core`, `packages/cli` and `packages/vscode` as empty packages with the manifests from the seed's Appendix A.2, plus `.changeset/config.json` (A.1) and `ci.yml` (A.4).
- Leave `release.yml` out: releasing is out of scope for this map.
- Done when `vp run -r build`, `vp check` and `vp test` pass on the empty packages, locally and in CI, and the result is on `main`.

## Context

- The devcontainer currently has Node 24.20 and no `vp`.
- `packages/cli` is scaffolded even though "What ships in v0.1.0 besides the extension?" may cut it; an empty package is cheap to delete.
- The answer should list the versions that were installed and every place the seed's [Stack](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#stack) table or appendix had to be changed to make things work.

nodes.title: Does @effect/vitest 4 work with Vitest 5 under Vite+?

nodes.body:
## Answer

The workspace is scaffolded on `main` in [`0178cf7`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/commit/0178cf7). `vp run -r build`, `vp check`, `vp test` and the `vue-tsc` typecheck pass locally (on Node 26.10.0 and also on Node 24.20.0) and in [CI](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/actions/runs/37057879804) (21 s).

The stack installs and works. The seed was wrong in small places, none of them structural.

### What the repo looks like now

- Root: `.node-version` (`26`), `package.json` (`packageManager: pnpm@12.8.1`), `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `vite.config.ts` (`fmt` and `lint` only), `tsconfig.json`, `.changeset/config.json` (A.1 unchanged), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (A.4 unchanged).
- `packages/core`: one placeholder export and one smoke test. `vp pack` emits `dist/index.mjs` and `dist/index.d.mts`.
- `packages/cli`: a placeholder `src/cli.ts`. `vp pack` emits an executable `dist/cli.mjs` and leaves `@hero-synergy/core` external.
- `packages/vscode`: `src/extension.ts` (host) and a minimal Vue app in `webview/`. `vp pack` emits `dist/extension.cjs` with core bundled in and `vscode` external; `vp build` emits `dist/webview`. `vsce package` produces a valid `.vsix`.
- `CLAUDE.md` carries Vite+'s agent instructions block.

### Versions installed

| Tool | Installed | Seed said |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node.js | 26.10.0 | 26 |
| pnpm | 12.8.1 | 12.8.1 |
| vite-plus | 1.0.0 | 1.0.0 |
| Vite (inside Vite+) | 8.3.1 | 8 |
| Vitest (inside Vite+) | 5.0.1 | 5 |
| tsdown (inside Vite+) | 0.23.0 | 0.23 |
| Oxlint (inside Vite+) | **1.85.0** | 1.86 |
| Oxfmt (inside Vite+) | **0.70.0** | 0.71 |
| oxlint-tsgolint | 7.0.2003 | not listed |
| TypeScript (root) | 7.0.2 | 7.0.2 |
| TypeScript (`packages/vscode`) | 6.0.3 | 6 |
| Vue / vue-tsc | 3.5.43 / 3.3.11 | 3.5 / 3.3 |
| @vitejs/plugin-vue | 6.0.9 | not listed |
| @types/node | 22.20.4 | not listed |
| @types/vscode | 1.100.0 | ~1.100.0 |
| @vscode/vsce / ovsx | 4.0.0 / 1.2.0 | 4.0.0 / 1.2.0 |
| @changesets/cli / changelog-github | 3.0.3 / 1.0.1 | 3.0.3 / 1.0.1 |
| setup-vp (CI) | v1.21.1 | v1.21.1 |

### Where the seed had to change

**Stack table**

1. Vite+ 1.0.0 pins Oxlint 1.85.0 and Oxfmt 0.70.0 exactly. The 1.86 and 0.71 in the table are the standalone releases, which Vite+ doesn't use.
2. `@types/node` is required and wasn't listed. TypeScript 6 and 7 no longer load `@types/*` automatically, so each tsconfig names its types (`"types": ["node"]`). I pinned `^22.18` to match the `engines.node` floor, so published code can't lean on Node 26 APIs by accident.
3. "It doesn't type-check `.vue` files" is true and has a consequence: `vp check` fails on `import App from './App.vue'` until the webview has a `*.vue` module shim (`webview/src/env.d.ts`). The real SFC check stays with `vue-tsc`. I confirmed both checkers catch a deliberate type error.

**Getting started**

4. `vp env pin` exists only in the global CLI. The project-local `vp` (from the `vite-plus` package) has no `env` command, so the pins were written by hand: `.node-version` and `packageManager`.
5. `vp migrate` on a repo with nothing to migrate writes the pnpm catalog and the `vite` override, and nothing else: no `vite.config.ts`, no agent instructions, and no `vitest` override (the seed expected all three). The `vitest` override isn't needed while nothing depends on `vitest` directly. I copied the agent block from `node_modules/vite-plus/AGENTS.md` into `CLAUDE.md`.
6. Don't run `vp migrate --full` here. It treats the repo as a pre-1.0 Vite+ project and adds tsdown compatibility settings (`deps.resolveDepSubpath`) and a duplicate shim. I reverted those.
7. Node 26 ships without corepack, so pnpm must come from somewhere else: the global `vp`, or `npm i -g pnpm@12.8.1`.

**Appendix A.2 (manifests)**

8. `packages/vscode` needs `@vitejs/plugin-vue` in `devDependencies`. Without it `vp build` fails to parse the first `.vue` file.
9. `packages/vscode` needs `"activationEvents": []`. vsce refuses to package a manifest that has `main` but no `activationEvents`.
10. pnpm 12 fails the install (`ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`) until build scripts are decided. `pnpm-workspace.yaml` now has `allowBuilds`: `@vscode/vsce-sign: true` (vsce needs its binary), `keytar: false` (a native credential store that token-free publishing never uses).
11. The root `release:notes` script is left out because `scripts/release-notes.ts` (A.6) belongs to the release work.
12. `vp check --fix` sorts `package.json` keys, so the manifests keep A.2's content but not its key order.

**Repository layout**

13. In `vite.config.ts`, the `pack` option `external` is deprecated in tsdown 0.23. The extension host uses `deps: { neverBundle: ['vscode'] }`.
14. The Vue app lives in `webview/` with its own `index.html` and `tsconfig.json`, and the package's Vite config sets `root: 'webview'` and `build.outDir: '../dist/webview'`. Pack first, then build, as the seed says: confirmed.

### Facts later tickets depend on

- **`vp check` formats Markdown, JSON and YAML too**, and CI runs it. A session that commits a glossary or ADR edit straight to `main` must run `vp check --fix` first or CI goes red. Excluded from formatting: `**/CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/seed.md` (frozen) and `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` (owned by `adc init`).
- **Formatting style** is single quotes and no semicolons, taken from the seed's code samples.
- **`vp test` at the root** finds test files in every package with no extra config. Tests import from `vite-plus/test`.
- **`vp run -r build`** builds in dependency order (core first, then cli and vscode in parallel), which is what lets packages type-check against core's built `.d.mts`.
- **Everything also passes on Node 24.20.0**, the devcontainer's default.
- **CI gets the global `vp` from GitHub**, not from `vite.plus`: `setup-vp` downloads `packages/cli/install.sh` from the `voidzero-dev/vite-plus` repo at the `v1.0.0` tag.

### The devcontainer

The devcontainer can't follow Getting started as written, and nothing here fixes that permanently:

- `vite.plus`, `viteplus.dev` and `voidzero.dev` time out from inside the container (npm, GitHub and nodejs.org are reachable), so the global `vp` isn't installed. I used the project-local `vp` instead (`pnpm exec vp …`).
- Node 26 was installed with `nvm install 26`. On this arm64 Debian image it needs `libatomic1` (`sudo apt-get install libatomic1`), which the image lacks.
- pnpm for Node 26 was installed with `npm i -g pnpm@12.8.1`.
- All three are lost when the container is rebuilt. The image (`ghcr.io/dbarjs/agent-devcontainer/node`) still ships Node 24, where the workspace works through corepack's pnpm and `pnpm exec vp`.

nodes.title: Which trackers and workspace shapes does v0.1.0 support?
nodes.body:
## Question

Which trackers and which workspace shapes must the Cockpit handle in v0.1.0, and which are left for later?

To decide:

- **Trackers.** GitHub through `gh`, local markdown under `.scratch/`, GitLab through `glab`, and "Other" trackers described in prose (the seed proposes an agentic collect step for those).
- **Workspace shapes.** A single repo, a multi-root workspace, and a workspace folder that is not the repo root.
- **Several maps.** A repo with more than one open map, and whether closed maps are shown.

## Context

- The seed's [Packages](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#packages) section gives core two adapters, GitHub and local `.scratch`, and lists GitLab and multi-root as open in [Not yet specified](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#not-yet-specified).
- Anything cut here moves to the map's Out of scope. The shape of a GitLab or "Other" adapter is fog on the map and may graduate from this ticket's answer.

## Answer

Decided with Eduardo in a grilling session on 2026-10-02. v0.1.0 supports two trackers and one repo per window.

### Trackers

- **In: GitHub on github.com**, with native sub-issues and native dependencies.
- **In: local markdown** under `.scratch/<effort>/`. It is the cheapest second adapter, and it keeps the snapshot from becoming GitHub-shaped: tickets are file paths, not URLs or issue numbers, and a claim has no person attached.
- **Out: GitLab.** Upstream GitLab is nearly all text conventions (`Part of #<map>`, a text blocker fallback on the free tier, an epic as the map on some tiers), and there is no GitLab project with a map to test against.
- **Out: "Other" trackers** and the agentic collect step. It would run an unattended agent with arbitrary CLIs on a timer.
- **Not promised: GitHub Enterprise Server.** The Cockpit tries any GitHub remote and shows the error if it fails.
- **Not promised: the text fallbacks** (`Part of #<map>` with a task list, `Blocked by: #n`). A map that uses them shows a drift warning.
- **Not promised: cross-repo relationships.** A map's tickets are its sub-issues in the same repo. A blocker in another repo is shown if the API returns it, and otherwise ignored.

### Which tracker a repo uses

- The **tracker doc decides**, classified by its heading (`# Issue tracker: GitHub`, `# Issue tracker: Local Markdown`) with no model. The Cockpit looks at `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` first, then follows the link in the `## Agent skills` block of `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`. An unrecognized heading is an unsupported tracker.
- **One tracker per repo.** If the doc says GitHub and `.scratch/*/map.md` files also exist (or the reverse), only the tracker the doc names is read.

### When the Cockpit can't show maps

One plain message per case, with no maps. Actions that need no tracker, such as `/grill-me`, stay available in every case.

| Case | What the Cockpit shows |
| --- | --- |
| No tracker doc | Leads with `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` |
| GitLab or "Other" doc | Names the tracker and says it isn't supported yet |
| GitHub doc, remote not on github.com | Tries anyway, and shows the error if it fails |
| `gh` missing or not logged in | Shows the fix (`gh auth login`) |

### Workspace shapes

- **One repo per window.** The Cockpit names the repo it is showing.
- **Multi-root workspace:** the first workspace folder, in workspace order, whose repo root has a tracker doc. If none has one, the first folder inside a git repo, which gets the setup message. Grouping maps per folder and a repo picker are out.
- **Folder inside a repo** (such as `packages/vscode` opened alone): in. The root comes from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; the tracker is read from there and sessions start there.
- **Folder holding several repos:** out. The Cockpit says no repo was found.

### Several maps

- **Every open map is shown**, each with its own frontier. A finished map that is still open stays visible, since that is where `/to-spec` is offered.
- **Closed maps are neither shown nor collected.**
- **On a local tracker every `.scratch/*/map.md` is shown.** A `map.md` has no open or closed state upstream, and the Cockpit invents none; a user hides a map by removing its directory.

### Local tracker details

- **Claim.** The glossary's Claim becomes: "A ticket marked as taken, made by the session before any work: an assignee on GitHub, a `Status: claimed` line on a local tracker." The Cockpit shows who claimed a ticket only where the tracker knows.
- **Sessions run in the main checkout**, without `-w`. Whether the Cockpit limits parallel local sessions is handed to [How do a session's worktree edits get back to main?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/5).

### Where this changes the seed

- "Multi-root workspaces, repos with several maps, and a GitLab tracker adapter" is no longer open: see above.
- The "Other" tracker paragraph of the scout (an agentic collect step) is cut.
- The Language entry for Claim assumed an assignment, which a local tracker doesn't have.

### No ADR

Each cut can be reversed by adding an adapter or a view later, so none of these meets the bar.

### Not yet done

The Claim wording above is not on `main` yet. This session's checkout was on another session's `prototype/map-rendering` branch, and the push to `main` was not permitted from here.

nodes.title: What ships in v0.1.0 besides the extension?
nodes.body:
## Question

Besides the VS Code extension, what does v0.1.0 ship?

To decide:

- **The CLI.** Does `@hero-synergy/cli` ship in v0.1.0, and with which commands (`snapshot --json`, `frontier`, `launch <ticket>`)? Who is it for: scripts, or agents inside sessions?
- **Core as a public package.** If the CLI is cut, is `@hero-synergy/core` still published to npm, or does it stay internal to the extension for now?
- **Nitro.** The stack names Nitro, but it has no role yet. Candidates in the seed are a locally served browser Cockpit and a docs site. Nitro 3 is still in beta.

## Context

- The three-package split is a `[P]` default in the seed's [Packages and releases](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#packages-and-releases); this ticket is where it gets challenged.
- The answer changes what "Which registries must be live for v0.1.0 to count as published?" has to cover.

nodes.title: Which registries must be live for v0.1.0 to count as published?

nodes.body:
## Answer

Decided with Eduardo on 2026-10-02. v0.1.0 ships the VS Code extension and nothing else.

| Item | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| `@hero-synergy/cli` | Cut from v0.1.0. No commands ship, and the spec removes `packages/cli` from the workspace. |
| `@hero-synergy/core` | Internal. It stays a separate workspace package with `"private": true` and no `vscode` imports, bundled into the extension and never published. |
| npm | v0.1.0 publishes nothing to npm. The `@hero-synergy` organization stays Eduardo's and unused. |
| Nitro | No role: v0.1.0 contains no Nitro code or dependency. Nitro is Eduardo's preferred backend framework, to be used if a server role appears. |
| Browser Cockpit, docs site | Neither ships. The README and the Marketplace page are the documentation for v0.1.0. |

## Why

- **The CLI has no audience yet.** Agents inside sessions follow the wayfinder skill and query the tracker with `gh`; they would only call `hero-synergy frontier` if Matt's skills or the tracker doc told them to, and the Cockpit is a lens that leaves both untouched. `launch` is redundant because the Cockpit shows the exact command for every action. `snapshot --json` would make the snapshot's shape a public contract while its fields are still undecided.
- **Publishing core is the hard-to-reverse direction.** npm versions are permanent and every export would need to stay stable while the scout and snapshot are being designed. Nobody is known to import it, and publishing later costs one release.
- **Core stays its own package** so that "no `vscode` imports" is enforced by the package boundary, its tests run under plain `vp test`, and a later CLI or public release is a manifest change.
- **Nitro's candidates fall outside v0.1.0.** A browser Cockpit is a second surface beyond the five capabilities and could not launch or follow sessions, which are VS Code terminals. A docs site isn't needed yet and wouldn't need Nitro.

## Changes

- [ADR 0001](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-publish-the-extension-as-dbarjs-hero-synergy.md) now says the scoped npm names are kept for later and v0.1.0 publishes neither (405d66b).
- [Which registries must be live for v0.1.0 to count as published?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/20) no longer lists npm as a candidate.
- No glossary change and no new ADR: every cut here is easy to undo.

## Against the seed

- The `[P]` three-package split becomes two workspace packages: `@hero-synergy/core` (private) and `hero-synergy` (the extension).
- The `[E]` "Publish the npm packages and the VS Code extension from GitHub Actions" narrows, for v0.1.0, to publishing the extension.
- The `[E]` stack list names Nitro; v0.1.0 doesn't use it.
- The npm steps in One-time setup, the npm publish step in `release.yml` (A.3), and the CLI and Core sections of `scripts/release-notes.ts` (A.6) no longer apply as written.
- On `main`, the scaffold still has `packages/cli` and publishable manifests for core and the CLI. Removing the CLI package and marking core private is build work for the spec.

## Not decided here

- How the release pipeline, the Changesets group and the release notes change with one published artifact: that belongs to [Which registries must be live for v0.1.0 to count as published?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/20).
- Whether a script for running the scout outside VS Code is useful during development: a build-time choice, inside core if it happens.

nodes.title: How do a session's worktree edits get back to main?
nodes.body:
## Question

A Cockpit session runs in its own worktree (`claude -w <ticket-slug>`). Grilling tickets edit `CONTEXT.md` and ADRs inline, so those edits land in the worktree. How do they get back to `main`, and who cleans up?

To decide:

- Whether every session gets a worktree, or only some ticket types.
- How glossary and ADR edits reach `main`: a commit straight to `main`, a branch and PR per ticket, or something the Cockpit offers as an action.
- What happens when two sessions edit `CONTEXT.md` at the same time.
- Who removes worktrees, and what the Cockpit shows about them.
- The local `.scratch` tracker exception: the seed says to run without `-w` there, or claims land in a private copy of the map.

## Context

- See [Sessions](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#sessions) in the seed.
- Until this is resolved, this map runs on the standing rule in its Notes: sessions commit glossary and ADR edits straight to `main`. The answer here replaces that rule.
- The session lifecycle (resume, one live session per ticket, AFK tickets) is fog on the map and may graduate from this ticket's answer.

**Handed over from [Which trackers and workspace shapes does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/3#issuecomment-5961301950):** the local markdown tracker is in scope for v0.1.0, and its sessions run in the main checkout without `-w`, because a worktree would give the claim a private copy of the map. So parallel sessions on a local tracker share one working tree, glossary edits included. Whether the Cockpit limits them to one live session at a time is this ticket's to decide.

## Resolution

**Every ticket session runs in its own worktree and pushes its own edits to `main`; the Cockpit only shows worktree state.** Eduardo agreed to all eleven points on 2026-10-02. This replaces the standing rule in the map's Notes.

Recorded in [ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md), the **Worktree** glossary term in [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CONTEXT.md), and the push-back routine in [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CLAUDE.md).

### Decided

1. **The Cockpit launches and watches.** It never runs git (no worktree creation, merge-back or removal) and never writes to the tracker. The push-back convention lives in the repo's own docs; hero-synergy's README recommends it, nothing writes it into the user's repo. ADR 0003.
2. **Every ticket session gets `-w <slug>`**, grilling included: today's shared checkout had an uncommitted `CONTEXT.md` edit from one session and sat 3 commits behind `origin/main` under another, which is exactly the collision. Standalone actions (`/grill-me`, `/ask-matt`, chart a map) run in the workspace root without `-w`.
3. **Glossary and ADR edits reach `main` by direct push, no PR:** in the worktree, `pnpm install`, `pnpm exec vp run build` (core's types come from `dist/`, so `vp check` fails unbuilt), edit, `pnpm exec vp check --fix`, commit on the worktree branch, `git pull --rebase origin main`, `git push origin HEAD:main` at ticket close. Prototype work stays on `prototype/<name>`, research on `research/<name>`, both pushed.
4. **Concurrent `CONTEXT.md` edits** are accepted: the session that pushes second rebases and resolves the conflict. No serialization of grilling sessions.
5. **Local `.scratch` tracker: no `-w`.** `.scratch` is gitignored, so a worktree has no tracker in it; `.worktreeinclude` would only copy it, and claims would still land in a private map. The Cockpit shows a note that sessions share the checkout; no enforcement of one session at a time.
6. **The Cockpit shows each ticket's worktree** (read-only, via `git worktree list` and `git log main..<branch>`): exists, has uncommitted files, has commits not on `main`. The last one is "work that never made it back".
7. **Branch name is the native `worktree-<slug>`.** A `WorktreeCreate` hook would replace all of claude's worktree logic for the sake of a nicer name.
8. **The exit prompt is an accepted gap**, like Esc: every `-n` session, clean or not, asks keep-or-remove on `/exit`, and no hook sees it. The Cockpit shows time since the last status event.
9. **Removal** is claude's exit prompt (remove once pushed, keep if unpushed) or the developer's hand. Nothing removes a worktree automatically; leftovers stay listed with their state (point 6).

### Facts that shaped it

From the [worktrees doc](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md): `-w` creates `.claude/worktrees/<name>` on `worktree-<name>`, branched from the **remote** default branch (`worktree.baseRef: "fresh"`), so a session never starts from a stale local `main`. `--resume` returns to the worktree. Headless `-p` runs never prompt and leave the worktree in place. No built-in push-back or merge-back exists.

### Not decided here

Resuming, one live session per ticket, AFK tickets and the workspace trust dialog graduate to their own ticket on the map.

nodes.title: Do the status hooks report a session's state reliably?
nodes.body:
## Question

Does a small Claude Code plugin, loaded with `--plugin-dir`, give the Cockpit a trustworthy live status for a session?

Build the plugin from the seed's Appendix A.7 as a throwaway on a `prototype/status-hooks` branch, launch real sessions with `HERO_SYNERGY_TICKET` and `HERO_SYNERGY_EVENTS` set, and watch the events file.

To find out:

- Whether each of the six statuses in the seed's [Live status](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#live-status) table shows up when it should: started, working, waiting for you, needs approval, failed, ended.
- Where the mapping lies: questions asked through a tool, subagents, compaction, a resumed session, a killed terminal, a session that ends without `SessionEnd`.
- Whether plugin hooks really merge with a repo's own hooks, and what `async: true` does to ordering.

## Context

- This challenges the `[P]` default "live status comes from a plugin loaded into each session".
- It needs no scaffolded workspace: the plugin is three small files.
- Which side wins when the scout and the hooks disagree is fog on the map and waits on this ticket.

## Resolution

**Yes, with a corrected table.** A plugin loaded with `--plugin-dir` stays the source of live status. The seed's six-row table is replaced, because three of its rows lie in ordinary use. Eduardo accepted all four points below on 2026-10-02.

Prototype, recorded runs and the full write-up: [`prototype/status-hooks`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/tree/prototype/status-hooks/prototype/status-hooks) (start with `README.md`). Tested on Claude Code 2.1.287 in the Linux devcontainer only.

### Decided

1. **The plugin stays, with this table.**

   | Status | Source |
   | --- | --- |
   | started | `SessionStart` with `startup` or `resume` only; `compact` and `clear` don't change the status |
   | working | `UserPromptSubmit`; also `PostToolUse` and `PostToolUseFailure` |
   | waiting for you | `Stop`; `PermissionRequest` for `AskUserQuestion` |
   | needs approval | `PermissionRequest` for any other tool |
   | failed | `StopFailure`, with `error` as the detail |
   | ended | the terminal closing; `SessionEnd` is a hint |

2. **The plugin also hooks tool calls** (`PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`). It is the only way to say "working" again after an approval or an answered question. The cost is one background `node` process per tool call.
3. **Esc is accepted as a gap in v0.1.0.** No hook reports an interrupt, so the status stays "working". The Cockpit shows how long ago the last status event arrived. The transcript does record `[Request interrupted by user]`, if this ever needs fixing.
4. **The terminal closing is the source of truth for "ended"**, on every platform. `SessionEnd` fires on `/exit`, on `/clear`, at the end of a headless run and when the terminal closes, but not on `kill -9`.

### What the runs showed

- The plugin loads with `--plugin-dir` and no install step. Its hooks merge with the repo's own hooks, and they inherit `HERO_SYNERGY_TICKET` and `HERO_SYNERGY_EVENTS`, in a `-w` worktree too.
- `async: true` doesn't hold the session up, and the `SessionEnd` line is still written after the session exits. A `StopFailure` hook without `async: true` never ran in a headless session, so `async: true` stays.
- `Notification` with `permission_prompt` arrives 6 seconds after the prompt appears, five times out of five, and never if the prompt is answered sooner. It fires the same way for `AskUserQuestion`, in manual and auto mode. `PermissionRequest` fires at once and carries `tool_name`.
- `Stop` also fires while a background agent is still running; the hook input lists it in `background_tasks`. When the agent finishes, `UserPromptSubmit` fires again.
- `/clear` ends the session id and starts a new one in the same terminal. A resumed session keeps its id. So status belongs to the ticket and its terminal, not to a session id.
- Line order isn't guaranteed. Unloaded, all 63 events were written in the order they fired, 20 to 247 ms after firing. With every core busy, 4 of 20 sessions wrote `SessionEnd` before `StopFailure`, and `at` is the write time. The reader must treat `SessionEnd` as final for its session id.
- Nothing fires while the workspace trust dialog is open, or while `/exit` in a worktree with uncommitted files asks whether to keep it.

### Not tested

Windows and macOS; `StopFailure` types other than `model_not_found`; `claude --bg` sessions.

Which of the names hero-synergy wants are free, taken, or already owned by Eduardo, and what are each registry's rules for claiming them?

To find out:

- **VS Code Marketplace.** The publisher IDs `hero-synergy` and `dbarjs`, and the constraints on a publisher ID.
- **Open VSX.** The `hero-synergy` namespace, and how a namespace is claimed.

nodes.title: Which publisher ID and npm names?

nodes.body:
## Answer

Full findings: [`docs/research/name-availability.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/name-availability/docs/research/name-availability.md) on the `research/name-availability` branch. Checked on 2026-10-02, read-only and signed out.

| Name | Status |
| --- | --- |
| npm organization `hero-synergy` (the `@hero-synergy` scope) | Exists, with no public packages. Created 2026-10-02, 61 seconds before this repo, so it is almost certainly Eduardo's; the owner is not publicly visible. |
| `@hero-synergy/core`, `@hero-synergy/cli` | Not published. |
| Unscoped npm `hero-synergy` | Free, with no punctuation-variant collision. |
| Marketplace publisher `hero-synergy` | No public trace, so probably free. |
| Marketplace publisher `dbarjs` | No public trace, so probably free. |
| Open VSX namespace `hero-synergy` | Free. |
| Open VSX namespace `dbarjs` | Free. |

Rules that shape the naming decision:

- **The Marketplace publisher ID can't be changed once created.** It allows letters, digits and hyphens. A removed extension's name stays reserved forever.
- **The Open VSX namespace is the `publisher` field**, so one choice picks the name on both registries.
- **Open VSX ownership is a human-reviewed claim** (an issue in `EclipseFdn/open-vsx.org`); `ovsx create-namespace` only makes you a contributor. `dbarjs` qualifies directly because it matches Eduardo's GitHub ID. `hero-synergy` needs the Marketplace publisher of the same name to exist first, which fixes the order: Marketplace publisher, then the Open VSX claim, then trusted publishing.
- **npm treats a placeholder as squatting.** Holding the unscoped `hero-synergy` name needs a real package behind it.

## Against the seed

Nothing is contradicted. Two gaps:

- The seed doesn't say the publisher ID is irreversible, and its Appendix A.2 already hard-codes `"publisher": "hero-synergy"` while the question is still open.
- The seed's Open VSX setup treats that registry as independent of the Marketplace. For the `hero-synergy` name it isn't.

## Not verified

- **Who owns the npm organization.** Members are visible only when signed in. Eduardo can confirm with `npm org ls hero-synergy`.
- **Whether the Marketplace publisher IDs are truly unregistered.** A publisher with no public extension leaves no public trace; only the signed-in "Create publisher" form is definitive.
- **Whether npm would accept an unscoped `hero-synergy` publish.** Its typosquat detection isn't public.
- No trademark search was done.
The hero-synergy npm org is mine

nodes.title: Can one GraphQL query collect everything the scout needs?
nodes.body:
## Question

Can a single `gh api graphql` query return everything the scout's collect step needs for every wayfinder issue in a repo?

To find out:

- The GraphQL fields for sub-issues (parent and children), issue dependencies (blocked by and blocking), labels, assignees, body, latest comments, state and `updatedAt`, and whether any needs a preview header or a minimum `gh` version.
- How to select every issue with a `wayfinder:` label when labels cannot be matched by prefix.
- Pagination limits and the rate-limit cost of the query on a map with around fifty tickets.
- What the REST endpoints give that GraphQL does not, as a fallback.

Try the query against this repo's own map; the repo is public.

## Context

- See step 1 of [The scout](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#the-scout) in the seed.
- "Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?" waits on this answer.

nodes.title: Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?

nodes.body:
## Answer

**Yes.** Full findings, with the working query and a sample of its output: [`docs/research/scout-graphql-query.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/scout-graphql-query/docs/research/scout-graphql-query.md) on the `research/scout-graphql-query` branch.

One `gh api graphql` query returns everything the collect step needs, with no preview header. Run against this repo's map it returned all 20 issues in one request (1.6 s, 40 KB, 6 rate-limit points), with children, labels, assignees and blocking edges correct.

- **Fields.** `parent`, `subIssues`, `subIssuesSummary`, `blockedBy`, `blocking`, `issueDependenciesSummary`, `labels`, `assignees`, `body`, `comments(last: n)`, `state`, `updatedAt`.
- **Selection.** `repository.issues(labels: [...])` matches the list as an OR and ignores names that don't exist, so the scout passes the known label names explicitly. Prefix and wildcard matching work nowhere, search included. `repository.labels(query: "wayfinder:")` in the same request lists the wayfinder labels that exist.
- **Pagination.** Only the top-level `issues` connection paginates, at 100 per page. Sub-issues cap at 100 per parent and dependencies at 50 per relationship, so the nested connections fit in one page.
- **Cost.** 6 points per page of 100, against 5,000 per hour. The cost depends on the page size, not on how many issues exist. A refresh every minute uses about 7% of the budget.
- **REST.** It has no data that GraphQL lacks. Its only extras are conditional requests (a 304 is free) and a separate rate-limit bucket; as a fallback it takes 13 requests for this map instead of 1.

## Where the seed is wrong

- **`updatedAt` does not move when a parent or a blocker is added.** On [Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/16), `updatedAt` still equals `createdAt` although the parent and two blockers were added afterwards. So `updatedAt` is a safe cache key for interpreting bodies and comments only; relationships must come from every fresh collect.
- **"One query" holds per 100 issues.** Closed tickets keep their labels, so a repo with several finished maps needs pagination, and the seed's pipe into `claude -p` assumes a single page.
- **The seed's sample command passes no variables**, but the label names have to be passed explicitly.
- The ticket's premise that REST gives something GraphQL doesn't was wrong.

## Not verified

- **Map order.** Whether `subIssues` comes back in map order. It returned the tickets in creation order, which here is the same thing. The frontier's "first in map order" depends on this.
- **Closed blockers.** Whether a closed blocker stays in `blockedBy`. Every blocker was open at the time; the query selects each blocker's `state` so the scout can decide either way.
- **`updatedAt` on other events**, such as a new comment or a blocker closing.
- **A real 50-ticket map.** The cost is certain; time and size were estimated from another repo (100 issues took 6.7 s, close to GitHub's 10 s cut-off).
- **GitHub Enterprise Server** and cross-repository parents or blockers.

nodes.title: Which wayfinder conventions exist in the wild?
nodes.body:
## Question

Which conventions has `mattpocock/skills` shipped for wayfinder maps and tickets over time, and what does each one look like on a tracker?

To find out, from the history of `skills/engineering/wayfinder/SKILL.md` and the `issue-tracker-*.md` templates:

- Every version of the map body (section names and order).
- How a claim was expressed (a `wayfinder:claimed` label, then the assignee).
- The ticket types and their labels.
- How children and blockers are expressed when native sub-issues or dependencies are off (task list, `Part of #n`, `Blocked by: #n`).
- The local `.scratch` layout and the GitLab template.

The result is a catalogue of drift: each convention, when it applied, and how to recognize it.

## Context

- The seed's [The scout](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#the-scout) section lists the drift known so far. One case is already visible here: `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` in this repo still describes the older "Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog" body.
- "Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?" waits on this answer, and so does the fog around the snapshot's fields.

nodes.title: Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?

nodes.body:
## Answer

Full findings: [`docs/research/wayfinder-conventions.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/wayfinder-conventions/docs/research/wayfinder-conventions.md) on the `research/wayfinder-conventions` branch. Everything comes from the git history of `mattpocock/skills` (`main` at `d81f3a1`, 2026-09-29) and the installed plugin, 1.2.3.

Upstream has shipped three generations of wayfinder state:

1. **A single Markdown file** (the `decision-mapping` skill, 2026-06-15 to 2026-07-01), with tickets as sections carrying `Type:`, `Status:` and `Blocked by:` lines.
2. **An early tracker map** (2026-07-01 to 2026-07-05, never in a tagged release): a `wayfinder:map` issue with a Notes / Decisions so far / Fog body.
3. **The current tracker map** (since 2026-07-05, released in v1.1.0 on 2026-07-08): Destination, Notes, Decisions so far, Not yet specified, Out of scope.

What a program can rely on:

- **Map body.** Four heading sets existed within four days. Recognize the old ones by their H2 headings: `Fog` without `Destination`, or `Deferred`; today's body has `Not yet specified`.
- **Claim.** The `wayfinder:claimed` label lived for 39 hours on `main` and was never released. Since then any assignee is the claim. On a local tracker the claim is a `Status: claimed` line, and always has been.
- **Ticket types.** The four `wayfinder:<type>` labels arrived together and were never renamed.
- **Fallbacks**, unchanged since the start: `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body plus a task list in the map body on GitHub, and `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` at the top of the child body. GitLab always uses `Part of #<map>`.
- **Local layout.** `.scratch/<effort>/map.md` and `issues/NN-<slug>.md` with `Type:`, `Status: claimed|resolved`, `Blocked by: NN, NN`, and the answer under `## Answer`.
- **Decisions so far entries.** `- [title](link) — gist` up to 1.2.3; unreleased `main` writes `- [title](link): gist`.
- **Upstream disagrees with itself today.** All three tracker templates still name the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body, while `SKILL.md` uses the five current headings.

## Where the seed is wrong

- `wayfinder:claimed` was never in a tagged release, so legacy claim labels are a rare case, not a common one.
- No tracker ever had a three-type label set: `task` is older than the labels.
- "The assignee is the claim" does not hold on a local tracker.
- The collect step can't assume `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`: since v1.1.0 upstream finds the tracker doc through the pointer in `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`.
- "Labels decide what the scout sees" is too strong: setup never creates the labels, a GitLab map may be an epic, and a local tracker has no labels.

## Not verified

- How common each legacy form is on real trackers: only upstream history and this repo's own map were read.
- The exact task-list syntax of the sub-issue fallback: upstream never writes it out.

nodes.title: How do VS Code terminals and Claude Code hooks behave on Windows?
nodes.body:
## Question

What breaks, or needs different handling, when the Cockpit launches sessions and reads status events on Windows?

To find out:

- How Claude Code runs on Windows today (native, WSL, Git Bash) and what that means for the `claude` command an extension spawns.
- How a VS Code terminal created by an extension passes a command with a quoted slash-command argument and environment variables across PowerShell, cmd and Git Bash.
- Whether exec-form hooks (`command: node`, `args`) and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` paths work on Windows.
- Whether appending to and watching the events file behaves the same there.

## Context

- See [Sessions](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#sessions) and [Live status](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#live-status) in the seed.
- "Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?" waits on this answer.

nodes.title: Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?

nodes.body:
## Answer

Full findings, with twelve concrete Windows test items: [`docs/research/windows-behavior.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/windows-behavior/docs/research/windows-behavior.md) on the `research/windows-behavior` branch. This was reading only; nothing was run on Windows.

What breaks or needs different handling:

- **How `claude` is installed changes how it can be spawned.** Claude Code runs natively (PowerShell or cmd; Git Bash is optional since 2.1.120) or inside WSL. The native install is `claude.exe`, but an npm install is a `claude.cmd` / `claude.ps1` shim, which Node's `child_process` can't spawn without a shell. This affects the scout as well as sessions.
- **The seed's launch command is bash syntax.** `sendText` does no quoting, and PowerShell, cmd and Git Bash each quote the ticket title and the prompt differently.
- **Running `claude` as the terminal's process avoids the quoting.** With `shellPath: 'claude'` and a `shellArgs` array, VS Code resolves the binary through `PATH` and node-pty quotes each argument, so no shell is involved.
- **Git Bash may rewrite the `/wayfinder …` prompt** into a Windows path, because of MSYS argument conversion.
- **Environment variables are fine.** `TerminalOptions.env` is shell-independent and hooks inherit the session's environment.
- **The hook shape in the seed is the one the docs recommend for Windows.** Exec-form `node` with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/report.mjs` needs Claude Code 2.1.139 or later and a real `node.exe` on `PATH`.
- **`CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS`** (2.1.280 and later) can replace `--plugin-dir "<path>"` and remove one quoted path.
- **`SessionEnd` probably never fires when a terminal is closed.** Windows kills the process forcefully, so "ended" should come from `window.onDidCloseTerminal`.
- **Watching the events file needs care.** Appending behaves the same as elsewhere, but watcher events are coalesced and can be dropped, so read from a byte offset, add a slow poll, and create the file before watching.
- **WSL remote windows behave as Linux.** Claude Code and Node must be installed inside the distribution.

## Against the seed

Nothing contradicts a seed decision. The gaps:

- The Sessions command doesn't say whether it is typed into a shell or run as the terminal's process.
- "SessionEnd means ended" can't be the only source of that status.
- The status plugin needs Claude Code 2.1.139 or later and `node` on `PATH`; the seed states neither, and Claude Code itself doesn't require Node.
- The scout example is a bash pipeline and needs a rule for npm `.cmd` installs. An open user report says `claude.cmd` broke a `--json-schema` call that `claude.exe` handled.

## Needs a real Windows test

- Whether exec-form hooks really bypass Git Bash: the maintainer's confirmation was on Linux, and two user reports describe arguments being re-parsed.

nodes.body:
## Question

Which VS Code API version does each fork currently ship, and what is the lowest `engines.vscode` that still gives the Cockpit the APIs it needs?

To find out:

- The VS Code version behind the current Cursor, Windsurf and VSCodium releases, and how far each usually lags.
- When the APIs the Cockpit relies on landed: webview views, extension-created terminals with a name, icon, environment and editor-area location, and file watching.
- How `@types/vscode` should be pinned against the chosen floor.

## Context

- The seed's manifest uses `^1.100.0` as a placeholder; see [Not yet specified](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#not-yet-specified).
- "Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?" waits on this answer.

nodes.title: Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?

nodes.body:
## Answer

Full findings: [`docs/research/fork-vscode-versions.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/fork-vscode-versions/docs/research/fork-vscode-versions.md) on the `research/fork-vscode-versions` branch. Everything was read on 2026-10-02; nothing was run inside any fork.

| Editor | Current release | VS Code version it declares |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VS Code | 1.140.0 (2026-09-30) | 1.140.0 |
| VSCodium | 1.135.06055 | 1.135.0 |
| Cursor | 3.23.12 | 1.128.0 |
| Windsurf (named Devin Desktop since 2026-06-02) | 3.10.48 | 1.126.0 |

**Recommended floor: `"engines": { "vscode": "^1.105.0" }` with `"@types/vscode": "~1.105.0"`.**

- **Node sets the floor, not the APIs.** Every API the Cockpit needs exists by VS Code 1.93. But VS Code 1.100 runs extensions on Node 20.19, below the `>=22.18` the seed sets for the core package the extension bundles. 1.104 is the first on Node 22.18, and 1.105 is the first such version that the forks actually shipped.
- **The floor can't go above 1.126**, the version Windsurf is on. `^1.125.0` with `~1.125.0` is the alternative if a Node 24 extension host is wanted; it drops fork builds from before July 2026.
- **When each API landed.** `createFileSystemWatcher` 1.0, `TerminalOptions.name` 1.9, `env` 1.18, `WebviewView` 1.50, `iconPath` 1.58, `color` 1.60, `location` (terminal in the editor area) 1.64, `isTransient` 1.65, shell integration 1.93. Watching a path outside the workspace needs a `RelativePattern` (1.64).
- **How the forks lag.** VS Code has shipped weekly since 1.111 (March 2026), so a gap of N versions is about N weeks. Cursor and Windsurf rebase irregularly: they land 2 to 7 weeks behind, then drift to 6.5 to 8.5 months. VSCodium follows within two weeks but now skips most weekly releases.
- **Pin `@types/vscode` with a tilde.** vsce 4.0.0 fails packaging if the types' major.minor exceeds `engines.vscode`, but it only reads the manifest string, so a caret range passes and still installs 1.140 types.
- **`@types/vscode` is no longer published for every release.** After 1.110 only some versions exist (1.115, 1.116, 1.118, 1.120, 1.125, 1.134, 1.136, 1.137, 1.138, 1.140), so a pin such as `~1.126.0` resolves to nothing.

## Against the seed

- The placeholder `^1.100.0` conflicts with the seed's own Node requirement, as above.
- "Windsurf" is now Devin Desktop.

## Not verified

- **Behavior inside the forks.** The versions are what each build declares, and Cursor staff say the editor internals "can sit on an older base" than the declared API version. Terminal in the editor area, terminal icons and webview views need a real test in each fork.
- **Cursor's exact switch dates.** Eleven builds were sampled; its changelog announces only one base change.
- **Windsurf's history** relies on its changelog, so an unannounced base change would be missing.
- **Node versions in the forks** come from Linux x64 builds only.

nodes.body:
## Answer

Full findings: [`docs/research/extension-integration-testing.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/extension-integration-testing/docs/research/extension-integration-testing.md) on the `research/extension-integration-testing` branch. This was reading only; no configuration was run.

The workable options:

| Option | What it covers | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit and component tests in `vp test` | Core, the extension's pure logic, and the Vue webview with `acquireVsCodeApi()` stubbed (happy-dom or jsdom with `@vue/test-utils`, or Vitest Browser Mode) | None beyond the stack, except Browser Mode's Playwright dependency |
| `@vscode/test-cli` with `@vscode/test-electron` | The extension host: activation, commands, terminals | Mocha only, a separate script (`vp run test:integration`), its own `.vscode-test.mjs`, test files bundled to CommonJS; about 30 s per CI run and `xvfb-run -a` on Linux |
| Playwright driving Electron | Real end-to-end, through the webview | Experimental per Playwright, hand-rolled fixtures, 4 to 12 minutes in CI |

Supporting facts:

- **Vitest can't run inside the extension host through any first-party route.** The official CLI "exclusively uses Mocha". The one community pool for Vitest is immature (version 0.1.3, built on an experimental API, older than Vitest 5).
- **Extension-host tests run on VS Code's bundled Node**, not Node 26: 20.19 at VS Code 1.100.
- **Webview contents can't be reached from extension-host tests.**
- **Every surveyed extension** (vitest-dev/vscode, oxc-vscode, cline, vscode-copilot-chat) uses Mocha through `vscode-test` for the host and Vitest for everything else. None uses WebdriverIO, ExTester or the Vitest pool.
- **CI.** xvfb is preinstalled on `ubuntu-latest`. The VS Code download is about 349 MB and most repos don't cache it.

## Against the seed

- **"Use `vp` for everything" can't cover extension-host tests.** They need Mocha started by `vscode-test`, launched through `vp run`, not `vp test`.
- **New dependencies.** `@vscode/test-cli`, `@vscode/test-electron` and `@types/mocha` are outside the Stack table, so the working agreement calls for an ADR.
- **The CI workflow has no display server**; an integration step needs `xvfb-run -a`.
- **Compiled tests need their own output directory**, because `dist` is cleaned by `vp pack` and shipped through `files`.

Two findings outside this ticket, for [Scaffold the workspace](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/2):

- npm's `vite-plus@1.0.0` pins Oxlint 1.85.0, Oxfmt 0.70.0 and Vitest 5.0.1, while the seed's Stack table says Oxlint 1.86 and Oxfmt 0.71.
- Vitest 5 no longer searches parent directories for a config, which matters when running `vp test` from a package subdirectory.

## Not verified

- Whether `vp pack` with an array `pack` block produces test files that `vscode-test` can load: this is a sketch from docs and source.
- Whether the community Vitest pool works with Vitest 5 or under `vp test`.
- Whether ESM test files load in `vscode-test`.
- CI timings come from two or three recent public runs per repo.

nodes.title: Scaffold the workspace
zod or Effect Schema for the snapshot?

nodes.body:
## Answer

**Yes.** `@effect/vitest` 4.0.0 runs under the Vitest 5.0.1 that Vite+ 1.0.0 bundles, with no override and no peer-dependency warning.

### What was done

On the throwaway branch [`task/effect-vitest`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/tree/task/effect-vitest) (commit b20ff17, not for `main`):

- Added `effect@4.0.0` (dependency) and `@effect/vitest@4.0.0` (devDependency) to `packages/core`.
- Wrote [`packages/core/src/effect.test.ts`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/task/effect-vitest/packages/core/src/effect.test.ts): `it.effect`, `it.live`, `it.effect.each`, `.fails`, `.skip`, `.prop` (from a Schema), the `TestClock`, the Vitest test context, and a shared `layer(...)`.
- Ran `vp run -r build`, `vp check`, `vp test` and the extension typecheck.

### Result

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `vp test`, Node 26.10 | 2 files passed; 12 passed, 1 expected fail, 1 skipped |
| `vp test`, Node 24.20 | same |
| `vp check` (format, type-aware lint, type check with TypeScript 7) | passes after `vp check --fix` |
| `vp run -r build`, extension typecheck | pass |
| A deliberately failing `it.effect` | reported as a failed test, exit code 1, the typed error printed |

### Facts later tickets can rely on

- **Peer dependencies.** `@effect/vitest` peers on `vitest >=5.0.0 <6.0.0` and `effect ^4.0.0`. `packages/core` does not declare `vitest`; pnpm satisfies the peer with the `vitest@5.0.1` that `vite-plus` already depends on. `pnpm peers check` reports no issues and `pnpm why vitest` finds one version.
- **One Vitest instance.** `vite-plus/test` is `export * from 'vitest'`, and `@effect/vitest` imports `vitest` directly; both resolve to the same copy (`expect` and `describe` are identical objects from either import). That is why it works.
- **Import convention.** Effect tests import `it`, `expect`, `describe` and `layer` from `@effect/vitest`, not from `vite-plus/test`. Plain tests keep importing from `vite-plus/test`. Both can sit in one file.
- **`effect@4.0.0` has no dependencies**, and `TestClock` lives in `effect/testing`.
- **Formatting.** `pnpm add` writes the new `package.json` keys in an order Oxfmt rejects; run `vp check --fix` after adding a dependency.

### One risk, no action needed now

The single instance holds because pnpm reused the Vitest already in the lockfile (5.0.1) even though 5.0.3 is the latest. If a later install ever resolves the peer to a different Vitest than the one Vite+ pins, `it.effect` would register tests with a second copy and they would silently not run. The "one Vitest instance" test in the spike catches this; the fix would be a `vitest` entry in the pnpm catalog or overrides matching Vite+'s pin. `@effect/vitest` 4.0.0 itself was built against Vitest 5.0.2.

### What this unblocks

[zod or Effect Schema for the snapshot?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/15) can now treat Effect Schema as testable in this toolchain; tooling is not a reason to prefer zod.

nodes.title: zod or Effect Schema for the snapshot?
nodes.body:
## Question

Which library models the data that crosses a boundary (the snapshot, config, webview messages): zod, Effect Schema, or both?

To decide:

- The seed's default is zod for boundary data and Effect for workflows. Does that mean modeling the snapshot twice once it flows through Effect code?
- The scout needs a JSON Schema for `claude -p --json-schema`. zod has `z.toJSONSchema()`; what does Effect Schema give?
- What the webview bundle pays for each choice.

## Context

- See [Stack](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#stack) in the seed. Both zod and Effect are requirements; only the split between them is open.
- A new dependency outside the stack needs an ADR, and this decision probably deserves one either way.

nodes.title: Does @effect/vitest 4 work with Vitest 5 under Vite+?

nodes.body:
## Resolution

**Effect Schema models all boundary data, and zod is dropped from the stack.** Eduardo's rule was: if Effect Schema completely replaces zod, use it. It does. Recorded in [ADR 0002](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-effect-schema-models-all-boundary-data.md).

### Decided

- **One library.** Effect Schema models the snapshot, config, webview messages, status events and `SKILL.md` frontmatter. This overrides the seed's `[E]` requirement for zod.
- **The webview doesn't validate.** It imports types only. The host and webview ship in one `.vsix`, and the host validates messages arriving from the webview.
- **Boundary data is plain JSON.** Timestamps stay ISO strings and schemas don't transform, so the decoded and encoded shapes are the same.
- **`@hero-synergy/core` doesn't export schema objects.** It exports types and functions that parse. Webview message schemas live in `packages/vscode`. Core stays private in v0.1.0 (see [What ships in v0.1.0 besides the extension?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/4)), so this rule is cheap to change until core is published.
- **zod as an unused peer is accepted.** `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` declares zod `^4.0.0` as a peer dependency, so it is installed if the SDK fallback is built. No hero-synergy code imports it.

### The ticket's three questions

Measured on 2026-10-02 with Effect 4.0.0, zod 4.6.5 and Claude Code 2.1.287.

- **Modeling twice?** No, with either choice. Effect code carries a zod-inferred type like any other type. The Effect modules the scout needs (child processes, file system, scheduling) don't import Schema; only the persistence modules do.
- **JSON Schema for `claude -p --json-schema`?** Both work on Haiku, each with one adjustment.
  - Effect: `Schema.toJsonSchemaDocument()` returns `{ dialect, schema, definitions }`. Pass `schema` with `definitions` moved under `$defs`. Shared definitions, descriptions, optional and nullable fields and records were all accepted.
  - zod: the raw `z.toJSONSchema()` output is rejected with `no schema with key or ref "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"`. It is accepted once `$schema` is removed, or with `target: "draft-7"`.
- **Webview bundle cost?** For validating one three-variant message (esbuild, minified):

| Webview validates with | Minified | Gzipped |
| --- | --- | --- |
| zod | 88.3 KB | 25.9 KB |
| Effect Schema | 74.5 KB | 24.9 KB |
| zod/mini | 23.1 KB | 7.6 KB |
| Nothing (types only) | 0 | 0 |

The glossary needed no change.

nodes.title: Which VS Code versions do Cursor, Windsurf and VSCodium ship?
How do VS Code terminals and Claude Code hooks behave on Windows?

nodes.body:
## Answer

v0.1.0 promises **VS Code 1.105 or later on macOS and Linux**, with native Windows and the VS Code forks reachable but untested. The whole promise is one **Requirements** section in `packages/vscode/README.md`, which the Marketplace and Open VSX render, plus the `engines` field.

### Operating systems

| Platform | Tier | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (arm64, x64) | Supported | Tested by hand before a release. |
| Linux (arm64, x64), including dev containers and SSH remotes | Supported | CI runs here; the devcontainer is the development environment. |
| WSL remote window on a Windows host | Supported, as Linux | `extensionKind: workspace` puts the scout, `gh` and `claude` inside the distribution. **This is the documented route for Windows users.** |
| Native Windows (PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash) | Best-effort | The code avoids every trap the Windows research found, the README says "untested on Windows", Windows bugs are accepted but never block a release. Install Claude Code with the **native installer**, not npm. |

One universal `.vsix`: the extension bundles no native modules.

### Editors

- `"engines": { "vscode": "^1.105.0" }` and `"@types/vscode": "~1.105.0"` (exists on npm; the `@types/vscode` gaps start after 1.110). The floor is set by Node, not by any API: every API the Cockpit uses exists since 1.93, but 1.105 is the first version that both runs extensions on Node ≥ 22.18 (core's own engine) and that every fork has shipped. Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) on 1.126 is the ceiling the floor must stay under.
- The pin is a tilde because vsce 4 reads only the manifest string: a caret would pass packaging and still install 1.140 types.
- **Cursor, Devin Desktop and VSCodium are not blocked, not supported.** The `.vsix` is published to **Open VSX** (namespace `dbarjs`, decided in #19), the README says "built for VS Code; forks are expected to work", and fork bugs are accepted, not promised. The fork research could not verify terminal-in-editor-area, terminal icons or webview views inside any fork, and Cursor staff say the internals can sit on an older base than the declared version.

### Runtime requirements the README states

- **Claude Code ≥ 2.1.139**, the release that added exec-form hooks (`"args": [...]`, no shell), the newest feature the status plugin relies on. `SessionEnd` is 1.0.85, `PermissionRequest` 2.0.45, `StopFailure` 2.1.78, `async: true` predates 2.1.23. `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS` (2.1.280) is not used: with the launch below, `--plugin-dir <path>` is never shell-quoted, so the variable would only raise the floor.
- **Node ≥ 22.18 on `PATH`** in the session's environment, because the hooks run `node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/report.mjs` and Claude Code itself ships no Node. On Windows that means a real `node.exe`. Handing the session the extension host's Node instead is a possible later refinement, not a v0.1.0 question.
- `gh` authenticated, for the GitHub tracker (already implied by #3).

### Decisions this forces on the launch

- **A session runs `claude` as the terminal's own process**: `createTerminal({ shellPath: 'claude', shellArgs: [...] })`, never a command typed into a shell with `sendText`. VS Code resolves the binary on `PATH` and node-pty quotes each argument, so the ticket title and the `/wayfinder …` prompt never pass through PowerShell, cmd or Git Bash (which would otherwise rewrite the slash-command as a path). Consequences accepted: the terminal closes when `claude` exits, which is the "ended" signal #6 chose; there is no shell for follow-up commands in that terminal; shell integration is unavailable. Feeds #21.
- **The extension resolves `claude` on `PATH` itself** for the scout and the launch, and on Windows prefers `claude.exe`; an npm `.cmd` shim can't be spawned by `child_process` without a shell, so it's best-effort only.
- **No gating on editor or OS.** The extension activates everywhere the floor allows, with no warning on forks or Windows. On activation it writes `vscode.env.appName`, `appHost`, the VS Code version, `process.platform` and the resolved `claude` path to the Cockpit's output channel, so bug reports from a fork or Windows carry what the research could not verify.

### Not an ADR

None of this is hard to reverse: the floor is a manifest number, the tiers are README text, and the `shellPath` launch is a few lines. The reasoning lives here; the `createTerminal` call gets a code comment when it's built.

### Out of scope, after v0.1.0

- The twelve-item real-Windows test from [`docs/research/windows-behavior.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/windows-behavior/docs/research/windows-behavior.md).
- Verifying terminals, icons and webview views inside each fork.

Sources: #11 and #12, and the Claude Code changelog read on 2026-10-02 (latest release 2.1.288).

## Answer

Decided with Eduardo on 2026-10-02.

| Name | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Marketplace publisher ID | `dbarjs`. Eduardo created the publisher during this session, so the ID is secured. |
| Extension ID | `dbarjs.hero-synergy` |

nodes.title: How does the Cockpit handle a session's lifecycle?
nodes.body:
## Question

A ticket has at most one live session, and a session lives in a VS Code terminal that can close, be resumed, or sit at a dialog no hook reports. What does the Cockpit do at each point?

To decide:

- **Resume.** When a ticket's terminal closes, what the Cockpit offers: `claude --resume "<ticket title>"` (which returns to the worktree by itself), a fresh launch, or both; and how the Cockpit tells "ended on purpose" from "terminal died".
- **One live session per ticket.** How the Cockpit holds to it when a ticket is claimed on the tracker but no terminal is open here, or a terminal is open but the tracker shows the ticket unclaimed. Status belongs to the ticket and its terminal, not to a session id, which changes on `/clear`.
- **AFK tickets.** Whether research and AFK task tickets run without a terminal in v0.1.0 (`claude --bg` with `claude attach <id>` later), or always in a terminal. Headless runs never see the worktree exit prompt and leave the worktree in place.
- **Local tracker launch.** The command without `-w`, with file paths in place of URLs.
- **Dialogs no hook reports.** Workspace trust at launch, and the keep-or-remove worktree prompt at `/exit` (accepted as a gap in [How do a session's worktree edits get back to main?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/5)): what the Cockpit shows while the session sits there.

## Context

- Graduated from the map's fog by [How do a session's worktree edits get back to main?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/5) and bound by [ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md): the Cockpit launches and watches, never runs git or writes to the tracker.
- The status table and the "terminal closing is the truth for ended" rule come from [Do the status hooks report a session's state reliably?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/6).
- See [Sessions](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#sessions) in the seed.

Context from [Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/17): a session runs `claude` as the terminal's own process (`shellPath`/`shellArgs`), never typed into a shell. So the terminal closes when `claude` exits, there is no shell for follow-up commands in it, and the local-tracker launch command is an argument array rather than a shell line. The extension resolves `claude` on `PATH` itself (preferring `claude.exe` on Windows).
